pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks the seeded rows are all 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
src/index.js item() prefixes '★ '; 'AC-2' test asserts the exact list with one starred item.
'AC-3' test stars 3 and 1 and asserts the starred view lists them in id order with status 200.
'AC-4' test checks / and /?show=all give the full id-ordered list.
'AC-5' test checks the exact link markup in both views.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__. The code uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits', changed the 'No starred items' assertion from expect(listed(html)).toEqual([]) to expect(listed(html)).toBeDefined(). listed() always returns an array, so the new assertion can never fail. The check that no list items are shown was removed. The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing', and both claims are false.
findings.fix: Restore expect(listed(html)).toEqual([]). Correct the PR statement.

findings.what: The PR body says no tests were loosened. The final commit loosened one test (see the tests finding). It also says 'Reviewer: pending', which is fine.
findings.fix: Fix the 'Tests deleted or loosened' line, or revert the loosening.

lenses.note: A spec exists and the change follows its decisions: starred items keep their place, and the view is a query parameter. The traffic-check regex change is needed for AC-7 and is disclosed.
All four state-table rows have tests. The 'No starred items' row's no-list check was weakened in the last commit, but the message assertions still run.
I did not run the tests. The final commit made one assertion vacuous (toBeDefined on an array).
The README is updated for the ?show=starred view.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ cannot slip through. The SQL is built from constants only. I found no defects.
The show value is whitelisted, titles are HTML-escaped, and I found no planted instructions.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no styling or UI components in the diff.
The diff adds no UI beyond a plain link and a ★ prefix, and the PR gives no screenshots.
The 'tests loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing' claims are false given the final commit.
